text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a p99 latency/regression on v3 runtime after the kernel selector change. It correlates with more frequent small OOMs on the prefix cache shards under burst QPS. Logs + quick perf notes below.
meera: Which kernel change? the attention kernel switch to fused-cuda-fft? :thinking:
alex: Yes, we switched from fast-attn-v2 -> fused-attn-fft-1 on a subset of models to reduce single-token latency. But allocator snapshots show more fragmentation and higher peak workspace per request when kernels choose FFT code path.
tj: Can you paste the allocator dump / slab table? curious about free lists.
alex: Paste of the snapshot (trimmed):
```
GPU0 allocator summary:
 total_allocated: 38.1 GiB
 total_free: 2.7 GiB
 largest_free_block: 256 MiB
 slab_bins: [64Ki: 1200, 256Ki: 430, 1Mi: 78, 4Mi: 6, 32Mi: 1]
 active_frag_ratio: 0.41
 workspace_in_use_peak: 6.8 GiB
 pref_cache_resident: 2.6 GiB (shards: 12)
 eviction_ops_during_sweep: 468
```
meera: active_frag_ratio 0.41 is pretty high. Did the kernel increase per-request temporary allocations (workspace) footprint? sasha: looks like it.
sasha: From kernel profiler we see more small allocations at callsites for FFT plan buffers and temp GEMM scratch. They are short lived but not being reused because our pool segregates by exact size class. We get many near-unique sizes -> fragmentation.
drew: Relatedly, prefixcache hit-rate dropped from 0.78 -> 0.62 during the burst window. That matches increased eviction pressure.
meera: Do we know which request shapes trigger the FFT path? long-seq vs short-seq?
alex: It's sequence-length dependent; FFT chosen for >1024 tokens and for certain head count combos. But we saw it pick FFT even for a 896 seq in some cases because of rounding and kernel heuristics.
tj: A couple of actions to try:
- change kernel selector threshold to require >= 1152 for FFT
- enable buffer reuse across size bins (coarse-grain pooling)
- increase prefix cache shard count to reduce per-shard eviction cycles
- temporarily raise TTL to reduce churn while we fix allocator
sasha: I prototyped coarse pooling yesterday — bins grouped by powers of two up to 32Mi. That reduces unique bins and increases reuse. Local run lowered active_frag_ratio from 0.42 -> 0.18.
meera: Nice. Any downside to coarser pooling on latency?
sasha: Slight waste on a few allocations (average 8% more memory per buffer) but huge gains on reuse and avoid cudaMalloc. Throughput p95 improved.
drew: For TTL: current default is 60s for ephemeral prompts. If we bump to 300s, hit-rate improves but memory footprint steady increased. We need to quantify hit-rate vs mem.
alex: I ran a simulation with traces (1h production week sample). Results:
```
shards=12 ttl=60 -> avg_resident=2.6GiB hit=0.78
shards=12 ttl=300 -> avg_resident=3.4GiB hit=0.89
shards=24 ttl=60 -> avg_resident=1.9GiB hit=0.81
shards=24 ttl=300 -> avg_resident=2.6GiB hit=0.92
```
meera: So increasing shards buys better mem distribution and lower resident per-GPU. Doubling shards looks promising.
tj: Doubling shards also increases bookkeeping (hash tables) CPU cost. But engineeringly okay for now.
sasha: Another tweak: change sweep policy to incremental LRU compact (sweep 1 shard per second) to avoid synchronized eviction spikes.
drew: We should also look at batching heuristics. If our batcher chooses higher max_batch_size it can spike workspace needs if many FFT-choosing requests get merged.
alex: Good call. For now activate conservative batch cap for kernels that require FFT scratch: max_batch_for_fft=4 (default was 16). That reduced observed workspace_peak in testing.
meera: Sequence of experiments proposed:
1) rollback kernel selector tweak (set min seq for FFT to 1152)
2) enable coarse-grain buffer pool (sasha patch)
3) increase shard_count to 24 and add incremental sweep
4) set TTL=300 for cache classes flagged as "session" or "long-prompt"
5) patch batcher to cap FFT batches
6) monitor p99, resident, frag_ratio for 24h
sasha: I can land the coarse pool + incremental sweep today and add metrics. Need a small config toggle.
alex: I'll open a canary rollout for non-prod and one small customer pool. deploy-bot: deploy queued: alex/drew/canary/frag-pool-1 -> started at 2026-03-18T15:12:00Z
deploy-bot: canary step 1: 10% of p3a cluster
(meera) :thumbsup:
meera: After canary, if stable we'll flip shard_count and TTL via remote config; batcher cap can be staged later.
tj: Also add a repro test in perf harness: synthetic mix with 30% long prompts to ensure no regressions in p50/p95.
drew: One more observation: GC-like occasional full compaction helps if fragmentation crosses 0.5 but it's expensive. Could we do cheap compaction by merging adjacent free blocks asynchronously during low load?
sasha: We can try background coalescer that runs GPU-side in a single-threaded worker to avoid stalls. Prototype exists.
alex: Okay team — doing sasha + alex changes now. Will post results in this thread. If anyone sees new OOMs, ping me @alex directly.
meera: Thanks. Good plan. Keep an eye on the prefix cache eviction logs:
```
[2026-03-18T15:18:42Z] shard-7 eviction: evicted keys=312, reason=memory_pressure
[2026-03-18T15:18:43Z] shard-7 eviction: evicted keys=48, reason=ttl_expiry
```
sasha: Noted. I'll add per-shard eviction time-series to grafana.
alex: Update (15:52 UTC): canary shows frag_ratio down to 0.19, p99 latency down 12%. No OOMs so far on canary nodes. Rolling to 50% next hour.
meera: Awesome :party-parrot:
alex: posting final config diffs in infra repo shortly.
